When we arrived,I was immediately struck by the sheer level of noise.First of all,there were dozens of food stalls packed closely together,each with vendors shouting at the top of their voices to attract customers.They were calling out their special dishes,bargaining with customers,and giving instructions to their helpers.On top of that,many stalls had loudspeakers playing pop music to create a lively atmosphere,and the music from different stalls overlapped in a chaotic way.Add to that the constant chatter of hundreds of people walking,eating,and laughing,and you can imagine how deafening it was. questions.questionText: What kinds of places are usually noisy in your country?
questions.rawText: What kinds of places are usually noisy in your country?
questions.referenceAnswer: In China,the places that are typically noisy include night markets,train stations,and shopping malls during peak hours.Night markets are especially loud because vendors shout to attract customers and loud music plays from many stalls.Similarly,train stations are full of announcements,people talking,and the sound of trains arriving and departing.Also,karaoke bars and restaurants with live music are quite popular and can be very noisy.In big cities, construction sites are another common source of noise,especially during the day.

questions.questionText: What are the main reasons why some places become very noisy?
questions.rawText: What are the main reasons why some places become very noisy?
questions.referenceAnswer: I think the main reasons are population density and commercial activities.When large numbers of people gather in a limited space,the noise level naturally rises -just from conversations,footsteps,and movement.Besides that,businesses like shops and restaurants often use music or loudspeakers to attract attention and create a lively atmosphere.In some cases,noise is also caused by poor urban planning,such as building entertainment venues right next to residential areas.So,it's usually a combination of human activity and commercial competition.

questions.questionText: Which is generally better for people,a noisy environment or a quiet one?
questions.rawText: Which is generally better for people,a noisy environment or a quiet one?
questions.referenceAnswer: I'd say a quiet environment is generally better for most people's health and well-being. Studies have shown that prolonged exposure to high noise levels can lead to stress,sleep problems,and even heart issues.Quiet environments help people relax,concentrate,and think more clearly.However,I do think a certain level of noise can be beneficial in social settings- for example,a lively restaurant with some background music feels more cheerful and energetic than a completely silent one.So,it really depends on the context.

questions.questionText: Are quiet places always better than noisy ones?
questions.rawText: Are quiet places always better than noisy ones?
questions.referenceAnswer: Not necessarily.While quiet places are great for studyingg,reading,or sleeping,they may not be ideal for every situation.For example,many people actually enjoy noisy environments like music concerts,sports games,or festivals because the loudness adds to the excitement and creates a sense of shared energy.In those contexts,silence would feel awkward and out of place.So I think it's not about one being absolutely better than the other- it's about choosing the right environment for the right activity.

questions.questionText: How do people usually respond when they encounter noisy behaviour in public?
questions.rawText: How do people usually respond when they encounter noisy behaviour in public?
questions.referenceAnswer: It really depends on the situation and the person.In many cases,Chinese people tend to be quite tolerant and patient,so they may just ignore the noise or move to a quieter spot if possible.However,if the noise is extreme,like someone playing loud music late at night on public transport,some people might ask politely to turn it down.But generally speaking, people prefer to avoid direct confrontation unless the noise seriously affects them.I think this is partly due to cultural norms that value harmony and keeping things peaceful.

questions.questionText: Describe a time when you saved money to buy something you wanted.
questions.rawText: Describe a time when you saved money to buy something you wanted. You should say: What you wanted to buy How you saved money for it How long did it take you to save money And how you felt after you bought it
questions.referenceAnswer: I'd like to talk about a time when I saved up to buy a new laptop.This happened about two years ago,during my second year of university. My old laptop had been with me since high school,and by that time it was painfully slow-it would take ages to boot up and often froze when I had multiple applications open.Since I needed a reliable computer for my coursework,research,and even some light video editing as a hobby,I decided it was time for an upgrade.I set my sights on a mid-range laptop that cost around 4,500 yuan. Saving that amount was no small feat for a university student with a limited monthly allowance.So,I came up with a practical plan.First,I cut down on unnecessary expenses-I stopped buying takeaways and started cooking simple meals at home.I also gave up my daily bubble tea habit,which saved me quite a bit each week.In addition,I took on a part-time job as a tutor,teaching English to a neighbour's child twice a week.That brought in about 800 yuan per month,which really accelerated my savings. All in all,it took me about four months to save enough money.There were definitely moments when I felt tempted to dip into my savings for something else,like a nice meal out with friends,but I stayed focused on my goal. When I finally walked into the electronics store and bought that laptop,I felt an overwhelming sense of achievement and relief.It wasn't just about owning a new device-it was proof that I could set a goal and stick to it.Every time I use that laptop now,I'm reminded of the effort I put in,and that makes me appreciate it even more.I also felt much more confident about my ability to manage money wisely in the future.

questions.questionText: Should schools teach children how to manage money?
questions.rawText: Should schools teach children how to manage money?
questions.referenceAnswer: Yes,I think schools definitely have a role to play in teaching children about money management.Most children don't naturally understand concepts like budgeting,saving,or the value of money unless they're taught explicitly.By including financial literacy in the school curriculum,children can learn essential life skills from an early age-for example,how to plan a budget or understand the difference between needs and wants.However,I believe schools shouldn't be solely responsible for this;parents should also play an active role at home.

questions.questionText: Should parents encourage their children to spend money freely or to be careful with it?
questions.rawText: Should parents encourage their children to spend money freely or to be careful with it?
questions.referenceAnswer: I think parents should definitely encourage their children to be careful with money rather than spend freely.Teaching children to be mindful of their spending helps them develop a healthy attitude towards money.However,I don't think parents should be overly strict either,because that might make children feel deprived or rebellious.Instead,they could give their children a small allowance and guide them to manage it themselves,allowing them to make mistakes and learn from them.It's about a between control and freedom.

questions.questionText: Is it easier to teach teenagers how to manage money when they are 16 or 17 years old?
questions.rawText: Is it easier to teach teenagers how to manage money when they are 16 or 17 years old?
questions.referenceAnswer: I would say yes,it is easier to teach money management to 16-or 17-year-olds compared to younger children,because by that age they have a better understanding of abstract concepts and have more real-life experience with spending.They may already have part-time jobs,receive a regular allowance,or need to budget for school expenses,which gives them practical context to apply what they learn.However,I think it's a gradual process,not something that should start at that age -ideally,we should introduce basic concepts much earlier and build upon them as children grow.

questions.questionText: Do you think which one is easier,saving money or spending money?
questions.rawText: Do you think which one is easier,saving money or spending money?
questions.referenceAnswer: Well,I think it's clearly much easier to spend money than to save it.Spending feels good and immediate-you get a product or an experience right away,which triggers instant pleasure.Saving,on the other hand,requires discipline,patience,and the ability to delay gratification,which is not easy for most people.That's why many people,including adults, struggle with saving.However,I think once you form a saving habit,it becomes easier over time.So in short,spending is easier in the moment,but saving is more rewarding in the long run.

When you arrive,the first thing that strikes you is the crystal-clear lake,surrounded by lush green hills.The water is so clean that you can see the pebbles at the bottom.Along the shore, there's a well-maintained walking trail lined with tall pine trees and colourful wildflowers.In the distance,you can see birds gliding over the water and hear the gentle sound of wind rustling through the leaves.It's completely different from the concrete jungle of the city. questions.questionText: What kind of people like to visit natural places?
questions.rawText: What kind of people like to visit natural places?
questions.referenceAnswer: I think people who visit natural places are usually those who lead busy,stressful lives and need a break from the fast pace of city life.For example,office workers often go to natural spots on weekends to unwind and recharge.Also,nature lovers,photographers,and hikers are naturally drawn to these places because they appreciate the beauty and tranquillity. Interestingly,I've also noticed that many families with young children enjoy visiting parks and lakes,as it's a great way for kids to explore and connect with the outdoors.

questions.questionText: What are the differences betweentween a natural place and a city?
questions.rawText: What are the differences betweentween a natural place and a city?
questions.referenceAnswer: There are quite a few differences.First of all,natural places are usually quiet and peaceful,with clean air and open spaces,while cities are crowded,noisy,and often polluted. In a natural setting,you can hear birds singing and leaves rustling,whereas in the city,the background noise is mostly traffic and construction.Also,the pace of life is completely different -in nature,everything feels slow and relaxed,but cities are fast-paced and full of pressure.Another difference is that natural places offer a visual feast of greenery and landscapes,while cities are dominated by concrete buildings and artificial lights.

questions.questionText: Do you think that going to the park is the only way to get close to nature?
questions.rawText: Do you think that going to the park is the only way to get close to nature?
questions.referenceAnswer: Not at all.While parks are certainly a convenient and accessible option for many city dwellers,there are many other ways to experience nature.For instance,people can go hiking in the mountains,visit botanical gardens,take a trip to the countryside,or even just grow plants on their balcony at home.Some people also enjoy camping by a lake or exploring wetlands near their city.So I think parks are just one ofmany ways to connect with nature-it really depends on how much time and resources people have.

questions.questionText: What can people gain from going to natural places?
questions.rawText: What can people gain from going to natural places?
questions.referenceAnswer: I think people can gain a lot from visiting natural places.Physically,it gives them fresh air and an opportunity to exercise,whether it's walking,hiking,or just strolling around. Mentally,it helps reduce stress and anxiety,allowing people to clear their minds and recharge their energy.On a deeper level,spending time in nature can also make people feel more grateful and humble,because it reminds them of the beauty and vastness of the world beyond their daily routines.Overall,it's incredibly beneficial for both physical and mental well-being.

questions.questionText: Are there any wild animals in the city?
questions.rawText: Are there any wild animals in the city?
questions.referenceAnswer: Yes,there are some,although not as many as in rural areas.In many cities,you can find wild birds like sparrows,magpies,and occasionally hawks.Squirrels are also quite common in city parks.In some larger cities near mountains or rivers,you might even see wild boars or monkeys wandering into urban areas occasionally,especially when their natural habitats are disturbed.However,most wild animals tend to avoid busy city centres because of the noise and lack of food sources.

questions.questionText: Do you think it is a good idea to let animals stay in local parks for people to see?
questions.rawText: Do you think it is a good idea to let animals stay in local parks for people to see?
questions.referenceAnswer: I think it depends on the situation.If the animals are native species and the park environment is suitable for them,then it can be a great idea because it gives people a chance to observe wildlife up close and learn about nature. However,if the animals are not suited to the environment,or if they're being kept in enclosures for entertainment purposes,then I think it's not a good idea.Animals should not be kept in unnatural conditions just for human viewing.Ideally,parks should protect existing wildlife rather than introduce new animals artificially.So,it's a good idea only when it's done with the animals'welfare in mind.

questions.referenceAnswer: I'd like to talk about my grandmother,who I believe is one of the happiest people I've ever known.She's in her late 70s and lives in a small village in the countryside,where she's spent her whole life.What makes her so happy,I think,is her incredible positivity and contentment.She doesn't have a lot of material possessions,but she never complains.Instead, she finds joy in the simplest things-a sunny day,a cup of tea with her neighbours,or the vegetables growing in her small garden.She also has a great sense of humour and loves to laugh.Even when things go wrong,she always finds something to smile about.For example, last year she had a minor accident and broke her wrist,but she just joked about it and said, "Well,now I have an excuse to rest!" I think the main reason she's so happy is her outlook on life.She lives in the present moment and doesn't worry too much about the past or the future. She values relationships over money, and she's always surrounded by family and friends who love her.She has a very strong sense of gratitude-she's grateful for her health,her family,and the simple life she lives.She also stays busy and active,which I think keeps her feeling fulfilled.She's never bored,because she always finds something meaningful to do. As for how I feel about her,I truly admire her.Whenever I spend time with her,I feel calmer and more positive.She reminds me that happiness doesn't come from having more things,but from appreciating what you already have.She's an inspiration to me,and I hope I can be as cheerful and content as she is when I grow older.

questions.questionText: What do people enjoy most about their secondary school years?
questions.rawText: What do people enjoy most about their secondary school years? 人们最享受中学时光的什么?
questions.referenceAnswer: I think what people enjoy most about their secondary school years is the sense of freedom and friendship.At that age,students are no longer treated like little children,but they don't yet have the heavy responsibilities of adulthood,so they feel a kind of freedom to explore their interests and personalities.Also,friendships formed during secondary school are often very special-students spend almost every day together,share joys and struggles,and create lasting memories.Many people also look back fondly on school activities like sports days,school trips,or just hanging out with friends after class.

questions.questionText: Can teachers tell when a child is unhappy?
questions.rawText: Can teachers tell when a child is unhappy?
questions.referenceAnswer: I think experienced teachers often can tell when a child is unhappy,but not always. Some children are very good at hiding their emotions,especially older ones who may feel embarrassed to show they're struggling.However,teachers who pay close attention to their students'behaviour can usually spot signs -for example, a usually cheerful child suddenly becoming quiet and withdrawn,or a student's grades dropping without any clear reason.That said,I don't think teachers can always know exactly what's wrong,but they can at least sense that something is off and offer support.

questions.questionText: Should teachers always know what their students are doing?
questions.rawText: Should teachers always know what their students are doing?
questions.referenceAnswer: I don't think teachers should always know everything their students are doing.Firstly,it would be impractical-teachers have many students and can't monitor every single activity. Secondly,and more importantly,students need some privacy and personal space to develop their independence.Constantly monitoring them could make them feel stressed and untrusted. However,I do think teachers should keep a general awareness of their students'well-being and academic progress.They don't need to know every detail,but they should be approachable so that students feel comfortable coming to them when they need help.

questions.questionText: How can the arts help spread positive emotions in society?
questions.rawText: How can the arts help spread positive emotions in society?

questions.questionText: Is it better to give handmade gifts or bought gifts?
questions.rawText: Is it better to give handmade gifts or bought gifts?
questions.referenceAnswer: Honestly,both have their merits.Handmade gifts have more warmth.Something you made yourself shows you spent time and effort.Especially for close ones—knitting a scarf for your parents or painting something for a friend—that kind of thought can't be bought.But handmade gifts also have risks—if it doesn't turn out well,the other person might not know. And some people just aren't crafty—forcing it can be awkward.Bought gifts are much simpler. More options,consistent quality,and you can pick their favorite brand.Especially things they wouldn't buy for themselves—if you give those,they'll be genuinely happy.But bought gifts can also miss the mark.They might already have it,or not like that particular style.At the end of the day,handmade gifts show effort—bought gifts show taste.Both are fine—it just depends on the occasion and the person.

questions.questionText: What kinds of gifts do people like to receive?
questions.rawText: What kinds of gifts do people like to receive?
questions.referenceAnswer: Honestly,what Chinese people like to receive really depends on how close they are to the giver.Between close people—like family and good friends—they prefer practical gifts.Like skincare products,gadgets,clothes,or nice food.People want something they'll actually use, not something that just collects dust.When it's from older to younger generations,red envelopes(cash)are the most popular.Especially during Spring Festival or birthdays—cash is the most straightforward and appreciated.Between coworkers or casual friends,people tend to give safe,neutral gifts.Like fiuit baskets,tea,or snack gift boxes.Not too expensive, and won't make the other person feel pressured.In recent years,experience-based gifts have become popular among young people,like concert tickets.

questions.questionText: Why do people give gifts on special occasions?
questions.rawText: Why do people give gifts on special occasions?
questions.referenceAnswer: Honestly,gift-giving is really about expressing feelings. Birthdays,weddings,New Year,promotions-giving gifts at these times says"I'm happy for you."Second is gratitude.Like giving something to a teacher at graduation or to a coworker when you leave—it's a way of saying "thank you.Third is maintaining relationships. Sometimes giving a gift isn't about a specific event—it's about letting someone know you still care.There's also a deeper reason—a sense of ritual.Gifts make special days feel special— more than just another day on the calendar.At the end of the day,gifts aren't essential,but they're carriers of emotion.

questions.questionText: Is it important to spend a lot of money on gifts?
questions.rawText: Is it important to spend a lot of money on gifts?
questions.referenceAnswer: Honestly,I don't think so.Expensive doesn't mean good.Spending 10,000 yuan on Something the other person doesn't need is worse than spending 100 yuan on something they actually want. Also,overly expensive gifts can pressure the receiver.It feels awkward to accept,and they can't afford to give something similar in return.What really matters is how much thought you put into it.When they receive it,they should feel,"You really understand me." Of course,expectations vary depending on the relationship.For family or partners,you'd put more into it—but between casual friends,there's no need to go overboard.At the end of the day,the value of a gift isn't on the price tag-it's in the intent.

At first,I didn't really know what to do.Without electricity,I couldn't continue my work, watch TV,or even charge my phone,which was already low on battery.So I just sat in the dark for a few minutes,trying to let my eyes adjust.Then I found a flashlight and some candles,and I lit a few candles around the living room.It was actually quite cozy in a strange way.I decided to call my family and we ended up sitting together in the candlelight,chatting and telling stories,which we rarely do because we're all usually busy with our own screens. My mum even brought out some snacks and we had a little impromptu family gathering. When I got bored,I also picked up a book that had been sitting on my shelf for months and finally read a few chapters. As for how I felt about this experience,I'd say it was surprisingly positive.At first,I was fiustrated because I couldn't get my work done and I was worried about the hot weather.But as the evening went on,I actually started to appreciate the forced break from technology.It felt like time had slowed down.I realised how much we rely on electricity for almost everything,and it made me think about how people lived without it in the past.By the time the power came back on,I actually felt a little reluctant to turn on the lights again.It was a simple but memorable experience that reminded me to slow down and appreciate the moments we spend with family.

questions.questionText: Describe a boring place you have been to.
questions.rawText: Describe a boring place you have been to. You should say: Where it is When you went there Who you went with And explain why you felt it was boring
questions.referenceAnswer: A boring place I have been to is a small town called Dalian in Liaoning Province.Actually,I've been there twice,but I have to say it was quite disappointing both times.I went there with my family during a summer vacation about three years ago.We planned the trip for months,expecting a relaxing beach holiday,but the reality was completely different.The main reason I found it boring was that there was literally nothing to do.The beach was crowded and dirty,and the weather was so hot that we couldn't even walk outside during midday.The town itself was very quiet—almost dead,with few restaurants or entertainment options.We spent most of our time inside the hotel room,watchingng TV or scrolling on our phones.The worst part was that everything closed early,around 8 or 9 PM.There was no nightlife at all,which made the evenings feel extremely long and dull.We had expected to experience the local culture and try fresh seafood,but most restaurants were either closed or offering overpriced,low-quality food.In the end,we cut our trip short and went home two days early.This experience taught me that not every tourist destination is worth visiting,and sometimes popular places are just overhyped.I'll do more thorough research before booking my next trip.
cuePoints: And explain why you felt it was boring

sets.setTitle: A boring place · 无聊的地方

questions.questionText: On what occasions do people feel bored?
questions.rawText: On what occasions do people feel bored?
questions.referenceAnswer: People usually feel bored when they have nothing interesting to do or when they're in a repetitive situation.For example,waiting in a long queue,sitting through a A boring meeting,or being alone with nothing to do can all trigger boredom.Boredom often comes when our brain is looking for stimulation but can't find any engaging activity.Sometimes even when we have free time,if we can't decide what to do,we end up feeling bored.The key is that boredom is a signal—our mind is telling us we need something more interesting or challenging.

questions.questionText: Why do students find their teachers'lessons boring?
questions.rawText: Why do students find their teachers'lessons boring?
questions.referenceAnswer: Students often find teachers'lessons boring when the teaching style doesn't match their learning preferences.If the teacher just reads from textbooks or speaks in a monotone voice for the entire class,students will naturally lose interest.Also,if the topic feels irrelevant to real life,students can't see the point of learning it.Some subjects are naturally more interesting than others,but a good teacher can make any topic engaging.I think the main problem is the lack of interaction and real-world examples.

questions.questionText: How to avoid feeling bored?
questions.rawText: How to avoid feeling bored?
questions.referenceAnswer: There are several ways to avoid feeling bored.First,try to find something interesting in whatever you're doing—even small details can make a difference.Second,change your environment or routine;sometimes a small change can bring new excitement.Third,challenge yourself with a new task or goal—having something to work towards keeps your mind engaged.Lastly,connect with people;social interaction is one of the most effective ways to kill boredom.Staying busy and maintaining a positive attitude also helps.

questions.questionText: Why do some people find playing on their phones boring?
questions.rawText: Why do some people find playing on their phones boring?
questions.referenceAnswer: Some people find playing on their phones boring because they're just mindlessly scrolling without any real purpose.They might be looking at the same content over and over,watching videos that don't interest them,or just swiping without enjoyment.Eventually,the screen becomes repetitive and loses its appeal.Also,too much screen time can cause eye strain and fatigue,which leads to boredom.The problem isn't the phone itself—it's how people use it.When used actively for communication or learning,phones aren't boring at all.

questions.questionText: Do you think it is difficult to become a doctor?
questions.rawText: Do you think it is difficult to become a doctor?
questions.referenceAnswer: Yes,I think it is quite difficult to become a doctor.The path is very long and demanding.First,you need excellent grades to get into medical school.Then,you study for many years—typically 5 to 8 years of university education.After that,you need to complete residency training,which involves long hours and intense work.Additionally,you must pass many exams and stay updated with medical knowledge throughout your career.It requires not just intelligence,but also dedication,patience,and strong communication skills.

questions.questionText: Do you think studying biology at school makes students healthier?
questions.rawText: Do you think studying biology at school makes students healthier?
questions.referenceAnswer: I think studying biology at school can help students make healthier choices,but it doesn't directly make them healthier.Biology teaches them about the human body,nutrition,and how diseases work.With this knowledge,they can better understand their health and make informed decisions.However,actually being healthy requires action—eating well,exercising,and good habits.Knowledge alone isn't enough.But biology education does provide a foundation for understanding health,which is a positive step.

questions.referenceAnswer: The business person I admire is Jack Ma,the founder of Alibaba.I know about him mainly from news articles,interviews,and his speeches online.He's become one of the most influential entrepreneurs in China and even globally.I first became aware of him around 2014 when Alibaba went public,making headlines worldwide.Since then,I've followed his career and found his story truly inspiring.He started Alibaba from his apartment in the 1990s when e-commerce was almost unheard of in China.Through hard work and vision,he built it into one of the largest companies in the world,revolutionizing how people shop and do business.He's involved in various businesses—primarily e-commerce through Taobao and Tmall,but also cloud computing through Alibaba Cloud,digital payments through Alipay,and logistics through Cainiao.His company has created millions of jobs and transformed China's digital economy.I admire him for several reasons.First,his persistence—he failed many times before succeeding,but never gave up.Second,his vision—he saw the potential of the internet before most people did.Third,he's generous—he's donated billions to charity and education through his foundation.Fourth,despite his successs,he's humble and often jokes about himself.What impresses me most is that he uses his wealth and influence to give back to society.He's not just a successful businessman,but someone who genuinely cares about making the world better.

questions.referenceAnswer: The decision I want to talk about is changing my major choice during university application.Initially,I had planned to apply for a business-related major,but eventually changed to English literature,which was quite a big switch for me.Originally,I decided to study business administration because many people said it offers better job prospects and higher salaries.My parents also preferred it,thinking it would lead to a stable career.I filled in my application forms with business as my first choice without much personal thought.However,a few weeks before the deadline,I changed my mind.I realized that while business might lead to good money,I wouldn't be happy spending years studying something I'm not passionate about.I love reading,writing,and analyzing literature.I started questioning whether I'd truly enjoy business classes.After much reflection,I decided to follow my heart and changed my application to English literature.Was it a good result?Looking back,I believe It was the right choice.I'm now studying something I genuinely enjoy,which keeps me motivated.Although job prospects might be less certain,I'm happier and more engaged in my studies.Learning about different cultures and literary works has broadened my horizons significantly.I felt relieved and more confident after changing the decision.It was scary to go against expectations,but I learned an important lesson:sometimes,you have to make decisions based on your own interests and passions,not just what others think is best.Following your heart might be riskier,but it's more likely to lead to a fulfilling life.
